ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the masses of objects A, B, and C are $m_{A}=m$, $m_{B}=m_{C}=2m$. Objects A and B are connected by a rope passing over a fixed pulley, and objects B and C are connected by a light spring with a spring constant $k_{2}$. A light spring with a spring constant $k_{1}$ is fixed to the ceiling at one end and connected to the pulley at the other end. Initially, objects A and B are on the same horizontal plane. The masses of the pulley, rope, and springs, as well as all friction, are negligible. A vertical downward force is applied slowly to object A. During the pulling process, the springs and the ropes connected to A and B remain vertical. The process continues until object C is about to leave the ground (A has not yet landed, and B has not collided with the pulley).

1. Find the deformation of the two springs before object A is pulled. Do not add any other content.
2. Find the distance the pulley descends when C is about to leave the ground.
3. Find the height difference between objects A and B when C is just about to leave the ground.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper end in the figure is the ceiling, the upper end of the vertical light spring k1 is fixed to the ceiling, and the lower end is connected to a pulley that can move up and down with the spring. The rope passes around the pulley, and the two ends hang vertically downward; object A is hung on the left end, and object B is hung on the right end. A vertical light spring k2 is connected below object B, the lower end of spring k2 is connected to object C, and C is placed on the ground. In the figure, A and B are initially at the same horizontal height. Reasoning: When A is not initially pulled, A is at rest, and the rope tension T0 = mg. The mass of the pulley is negligible, and it is pulled downward by the two segments of rope, so the elastic force of k1 satisfies k1 x10 = 2T0 = 2mg; therefore the initial deformation of k1 is 2mg/k1. The weight of B is 2mg, and the upward pull of the rope on B is mg; therefore k2 must exert mg upward on B, so k2 is initially compressed, with deformation mg/k2. When C is just about to leave the ground, the support force of the ground on C is 0. The weight of C is 2mg, so k2 must pull C upward, and the elastic force is 2mg; therefore k2 is at this time elongated, with deformation 2mg/k2. For the equilibrium of B: B is subjected to the upward pull Tf of the rope, the weight 2mg downward, and the elongated k2 pulls B downward by 2mg, so Tf = 4mg. The equilibrium of the pulley gives k1 xf = 2Tf = 8mg, therefore xf = 8mg/k1. The downward distance of the pulley is equal to the increase in the deformation of k1: xf - x10 = 8mg/k1 - 2mg/k1 = 6mg/k1. Find the height difference between A and B: k2 changes from the initial compression mg/k2 to the final elongation 2mg/k2, and the distance between B and C increases by 3mg/k2. C is still on the ground just before leaving the ground, so B rises by 3mg/k2. Taking downward as positive, let the downward displacement of the pulley be p = 6mg/k1, and the displacements of A and B be yA and yB respectively; then the unchanged rope length gives yA + yB = 2p. Also yB = -3mg/k2, so yA - yB = 2p - 2yB = 12mg/k1 + 6mg/k2. Therefore the height difference between A and B is 6mg/k2 + 12mg/k1.

method.method_draft: Direct free-body equilibrium method. First read the diagram as: ceiling spring k1 supports a movable pulley; a single rope passes over the pulley with A on the left and B on the right; B is connected downward by spring k2 to C, which rests on the ground. From the text use mA=m and mB=mC=2m, quasi-static pulling, massless rope/pulley/springs, and vertical rope/spring segments. Before pulling, draw FBDs: A gives rope tension T0=mg; massless pulley gives k1 x10=2T0, so x10=2mg/k1; B equilibrium requires spring k2 to push upward by mg, so its deformation magnitude is mg/k2. At the instant C is about to leave the ground, impose NC=0 on C, so spring k2 must pull C upward with 2mg; hence k2 deformation is an extension 2mg/k2. Use B equilibrium then to get final rope tension Tf=2mg+2mg=4mg. The pulley equilibrium gives final k1 deformation xf=2Tf/k1=8mg/k1, so pulley descent is xf-x10=6mg/k1. For the height difference, use the change of k2 deformation from initial compression mg/k2 to final extension 2mg/k2: the B-C separation increases by 3mg/k2, and since C remains on the ground up to lift-off, B moves upward by 3mg/k2. Then apply constant rope length: if pulley descends p, A and B displacements from their initial common level satisfy yA+yB=2p. With p=6mg/k1 and yB=-3mg/k2, obtain yA-yB=12mg/k1+6mg/k2.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中上端是天花板，竖直轻弹簧 k1 的上端固定在天花板上，下端连接一个可随弹簧上下移动的滑轮。绳子绕过滑轮，两端竖直下垂，左端挂物体 A，右端挂物体 B。物体 B 下方连接竖直轻弹簧 k2，弹簧 k2 下端连接物体 C，C 放在地面上。图中 A、B 初始处在同一水平高度。

推理：初始未拉 A 时，A 静止，绳张力 T0 = mg。滑轮质量不计，受两段绳向下拉力，所以 k1 的弹力满足 k1 x10 = 2T0 = 2mg，因此 k1 初始形变量为 2mg/k1。B 的重力为 2mg，绳对 B 向上拉力为 mg，因此 k2 必须对 B 向上作用 mg，故 k2 初始为压缩，形变量为 mg/k2。

当 C 刚要离地时，地面对 C 的支持力为 0。C 的重力为 2mg，所以 k2 必须向上拉 C，弹力为 2mg，因此 k2 此时为伸长，形变量为 2mg/k2。对 B 平衡：B 受绳向上拉力 Tf，受重力 2mg 向下，且伸长的 k2 对 B 向下拉 2mg，所以 Tf = 4mg。滑轮平衡给出 k1 xf = 2Tf = 8mg，因此 xf = 8mg/k1。滑轮下降距离等于 k1 形变量增加量：xf - x10 = 8mg/k1 - 2mg/k1 = 6mg/k1。

求 A、B 高度差：k2 从初始压缩 mg/k2 变为最终伸长 2mg/k2，B、C 间距增加 3mg/k2。C 在刚离地前仍在地面上，所以 B 上升 3mg/k2。取向下为正，设滑轮下降 p = 6mg/k1，A、B 的位移分别为 yA、yB，则绳长不变给出 yA + yB = 2p。又 yB = -3mg/k2，所以 yA - yB = 2p - 2yB = 12mg/k1 + 6mg/k2。因此 A 与 B 的高度差为 6mg/k2 + 12mg/k1。

method.method_draft: Incremental quasi-static stiffness/compatibility method. Read the image as a vertical load chain: k1 supports the movable pulley, the same rope tension acts on A and B, and k2 links B to grounded C. From the text, note the process is slow, so every small change is an equilibrium change. Establish the initial signed spring states: A equilibrium gives initial rope tension T0=mg; the pulley load is 2T0, so k1 initial deformation is 2mg/k1; B equilibrium with T0<2mg means k2 is initially compressed by mg/k2. Now work only with changes until lift-off. Use a signed k2 deformation s positive for extension. Initially s0=-mg/k2. At lift-off, C has zero normal force, so the spring must pull C upward by 2mg, giving sf=+2mg/k2. Thus Δs=3mg/k2 and, since C has not yet moved, B must move upward by 3mg/k2. B's equilibrium relation is T=2mg+k2 s, so ΔT=k2Δs=3mg and Tf=4mg. The massless pulley requires the k1 force to equal 2T, so the increase of k1 deformation, which is also the pulley descent, is Δx1=2ΔT/k1=6mg/k1. Finally use the rope length change about the descending pulley: ΔyA+ΔyB=2Δyp. With Δyp=6mg/k1 and ΔyB=-3mg/k2, solve ΔyA=12mg/k1+3mg/k2, so the height difference A below B is ΔyA-ΔyB=12mg/k1+6mg/k2.

图像描述：图中上端天花板固定一根轻弹簧 k1，弹簧下端连接一个滑轮；一根绳绕过滑轮，两端分别竖直连接物体 A 和 B。B 的下方通过竖直轻弹簧 k2 与物体 C 相连，C 放在地面上。A、B 初始在同一水平高度。

推理：缓慢拉动，过程可视为一系列静力平衡。初始时，A 平衡，所以绳张力 T0=mg。滑轮受两段绳向下拉力，总载荷为 2T0=2mg，因此 k1 初始形变量为 2mg/k1。对 B，重力为 2mg，向上绳张力为 mg，因此 k2 必须对 B 向上作用 mg，即 k2 初始被压缩 mg/k2。

取 k2 的形变量 s 以伸长为正，则初始 s0=-mg/k2。C 刚要离地时，地面对 C 的支持力为 0，弹簧需向上拉 C，大小等于 C 的重力 2mg，所以 sf=2mg/k2。因此 Δs=sf-s0=3mg/k2。C 尚未运动，所以 B 上升 3mg/k2，即 ΔyB=-3mg/k2（向下为正）。

B 的平衡关系为 T=2mg+k2s，因此张力增量 ΔT=k2Δs=3mg，末态 Tf=4mg。滑轮平衡要求 k1 弹力等于 2T，所以 k1 形变量增量，也就是滑轮下降距离，为 Δyp=2ΔT/k1=6mg/k1。

绳长不变，滑轮下降满足 ΔyA+ΔyB=2Δyp。代入 Δyp=6mg/k1、ΔyB=-3mg/k2，得 ΔyA=12mg/k1+3mg/k2。初始 A、B 等高，所以末态 A 相对 B 的高度差为 ΔyA-ΔyB=12mg/k1+6mg/k2。

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, the masses of objects A, B, and C are $m_{A}=m$, $m_{B}=m_{C}=2m$. Objects A and B are connected by a rope passing over a fixed pulley, and objects B and C are connected by a light spring with a spring constant $k_{2}$. A light spring with a spring constant $k_{1}$ is fixed to the ceiling at one end and connected to the pulley at the other end. Initially, objects A and B are on the same horizontal plane. The masses of the pulley, rope, and springs, as well as all friction, are negligible. A vertical downward force is applied slowly to object A. During the pulling process, the springs and the ropes connected to A and B remain vertical. The process continues until object C is about to leave the ground (A has not yet landed, and B has not collided with the pulley).

1. Find the deformation of the two springs before object A is pulled. Do not add any other content.
2. Find the distance the pulley descends when C is about to leave the ground.
3. Find the height difference between objects A and B when C is just about to leave the ground.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The upper end in the figure is the ceiling, the upper end of the vertical light spring k1 is fixed to the ceiling, and the lower end is connected to a pulley that can move up and down with the spring. The rope passes around the pulley, and the two ends hang vertically downward; object A is hung on the left end, and object B is hung on the right end. A vertical light spring k2 is connected below object B, the lower end of spring k2 is connected to object C, and C is placed on the ground. In the figure, A and B are initially at the same horizontal height.

Reasoning: When A is not initially pulled, A is at rest, and the rope tension T0 = mg. The mass of the pulley is negligible, and it is pulled downward by the two segments of rope, so the elastic force of k1 satisfies k1 x10 = 2T0 = 2mg; therefore the initial deformation of k1 is 2mg/k1. The weight of B is 2mg, and the upward pull of the rope on B is mg; therefore k2 must exert mg upward on B, so k2 is initially compressed, with deformation mg/k2.

When C is just about to leave the ground, the support force of the ground on C is 0. The weight of C is 2mg, so k2 must pull C upward, and the elastic force is 2mg; therefore k2 is at this time elongated, with deformation 2mg/k2. For the equilibrium of B: B is subjected to the upward pull Tf of the rope, the weight 2mg downward, and the elongated k2 pulls B downward by 2mg, so Tf = 4mg. The equilibrium of the pulley gives k1 xf = 2Tf = 8mg, therefore xf = 8mg/k1. The downward distance of the pulley is equal to the increase in the deformation of k1: xf - x10 = 8mg/k1 - 2mg/k1 = 6mg/k1.

Find the height difference between A and B: k2 changes from the initial compression mg/k2 to the final elongation 2mg/k2, and the distance between B and C increases by 3mg/k2. C is still on the ground just before leaving the ground, so B rises by 3mg/k2. Taking downward as positive, let the downward displacement of the pulley be p = 6mg/k1, and the displacements of A and B be yA and yB respectively; then the unchanged rope length gives yA + yB = 2p. Also yB = -3mg/k2, so yA - yB = 2p - 2yB = 12mg/k1 + 6mg/k2. Therefore the height difference between A and B is 6mg/k2 + 12mg/k1.
